author: Lennart Demes (ambientCG)
notes: Grey, heavily alligator-cracked weathered asphalt with dirt in the cracks: reads as a neglected rural lot. Made procedurally from a substance (PBRProcedural), not a scan, but looks photoreal. The crack network repeats visibly at 1.85 m, so break it up with the existing noise or grime, or mix it with road-asphalt. Albedo and normal are 2K; roughness and AO are 1K.

author: Dimitrios Savva
notes: Alternate. A real scan of patched, stained and crumbling asphalt with dark oily patches. The albedo has a strong brown cast, so desaturate it about 60-70% or multiply by a grey tint before use. 1K to save space.

author: Rob Tuytel
notes: Scanned, gritty grey highway asphalt with long longitudinal tar-sealed cracks. Neutral colour that tints well. Align the cracks with the road direction (V axis). Albedo and normal are 2K; roughness and AO are 1K.

author: Dario Barresi, Dimitrios Savva
targetMats: ground shader tConcA/tConcN (forecourt slab under canopy, sidewalk)
notes: Scan of weathered outdoor brushed concrete with stains, discolouration and pits. The albedo is warm beige-grey, and the MATS colour multipliers will grey it down. For canopyUnder (a ceiling), use a lower uvMul or just the normal and roughness maps. Albedo and normal are 2K; roughness and AO are 1K.

author: Dario Barresi, Charlotte Baglioni
notes: Scan of a painted concrete-block (CMU) wall with recessed mortar joints, drip stains and specks. The paint is a drab grey-green, so convert the albedo to luminance and apply the MATS paint colours. At the stated 2 m the courses come out about 0.46 m tall, larger than US 8x16 in CMU. For true 0.2 m courses, repeat it about every 0.9 m. On the pillars, the block lines may be unwanted, so the normal and roughness alone may be enough there. Albedo and normal are 2K; roughness and AO are 1K.

author: Dimitrios Savva
notes: Scan of dark tar with embedded light gravel, which matches a built-up tar-and-gravel flat roof. The roof is rarely seen up close, so it is stored at 1K. Poly Haven 'bitumen' (rolled roofing, 20 m tile) was the other option considered.

author: Lennart Demes (ambientCG)
notes: White paint over steel with chipped flakes that show grey bare metal and a little rust. Made procedurally (PBRProcedural). ambientCG gives no physical size. The chip scale suggests about 1 m per tile, which suits the existing metal: 1.0 in site.js. Because the base is near white, it can be tinted by the MATS paint colours. A paint mask (albedo luminance > ~0.8) would keep the chips and rust untinted. The source also includes a metalness map, which was not copied. Its roughness is low (painted gloss, mean 0.28). Stored at 1K because these are small surfaces.

author: Lennart Demes (ambientCG)
targetMats: ground shader (road shoulder / lot edge blend)
notes: Photogrammetry scan of dry brown dirt with mixed grey gravel and pebbles and a few dry twigs. Suits a dusty rural road shoulder. Albedo and normal are 2K; roughness and AO are 1K.

author: Charlotte Baglioni
notes: Scan of dead, straw-coloured matted grass with darker patches, a fit for dry acacia-scrub country. The current groundcover tile is 6 m (site.js), so using the real 2 m size (or about 3 m) will look more correct. Albedo and normal are 2K; roughness and AO are 1K.

author: Charlotte Baglioni
notes: Scan of deeply furrowed grey-brown bark with vertical fissures. Close to the rough fissured bark of an acacia or thorn tree. The grain runs along V, so map V up the trunk. Stored at 1K.

author: Rob Tuytel
notes: Scan of common red brick in stretcher bond with grey mortar, about 20 courses per 1.4 m, which is close to real scale. The current brick material uses the stucco tex with a paint tint; the albedo should be used as-is (drop the paint tint). Stored at 1K because the chimney is small.
